newsitem.title: GERMANY: German economy slows in the fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: German economy slows in the fourth quarter.

text.p: German economic output declined 0.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the previous quarter due mainly to weak consumer spending, the Bundesbank said Thursday.

Fourth quarter gross domestic product was 770.4 billion marks ($456.8 billion), down slightly from 772 billion marks ($457.8 billion) in the previous quarter, but 1.6-percent higher than the year-earlier quarter, the central bank said.
Growth in the third quarter was 0.8 percent from the previous quarter and 1.9 percent year-on-year.
Economists said the data were weaker than expected.
They said the fourth-quarter data reinforced views that 1997 economic growth was likely to fall short of the government's projection of 2.5 percent.
Weak consumer spending was the main reason for the fourth-quarter economic output decline, while a surge in imports also outweighed a rise in exports.
"Private comsumption suffered from high unemployment and a small decline in disposable income," said analyst Holger Fahrinkrug at UBS in Frankfurt, who sees 1997 growth at 2.0 percent.
